data.title: Prestige launches 260 flats in North Bengaluru; 2 BHKs start at ₹1.73 crore
data.description:
Prestige Estates Projects has launched Prestige Avon on Thanisandra Main Road in North Bengaluru, with prices starting at ₹1.73 crore for a 2 BHK apartment and a quoted base rate of ₹13,300–14,500 per sq ft.
 
 The 3 BHK homes are priced from ₹2.30 crore, while the larger 3.5 BHK configuration with a maid's room starts at ₹2.78 crore, before additional charges.
 
Spread across approximately three acres, the project will comprise 260 apartments with a total saleable area of about 4 lakh sq ft. Prestige has estimated its gross development value (GDV) at ₹550 crore, according to its November 20 stock-exchange announcement. 
 
Dividing the estimated GDV by the stated saleable area gives an indicative value of approximately ₹13,750 per sq ft. 
 
 
The apartments range from approximately 1,306 sq ft to 2,160 sq ft and are being offered in 2 and 3 BHK configurations, including select layouts with dedicated home-office spaces. The developer in a statement said the project is aimed at buyers seeking flexible living arrangements that accommodate both work and personal requirements.
 
How does Avon compare with Prestige's earlier Bengaluru launches?
 
The indicative base rate of ₹13,300–14,500 per sq ft places Avon in a similar price bracket to some of Prestige's recent residential developments in Bengaluru.
 
For instance, Housing.com lists an average price of approximately ₹14,990 per sq ft for Prestige Somerville in Whitefield, which was launched in April 2024. The project offers 2, 3, 3.5 and 4 BHK apartments, with sizes ranging from 1,203 sq ft to 3,543 sq ft.
 
Prestige Pine Forest, another Whitefield project launched in September 2024, has an average listed price of around ₹13,910 per sq ft, according to the property portal. The project offers larger 3 and 4 BHK apartments and penthouses.
 
Prestige Camden Gardens, located in the North Bengaluru region, has an average listed price of approximately ₹15,590 per sq ft on Housing.com. Launched in May 2024, it offers 3 and 4 BHK apartments. 
 
North Bengaluru remains a key residential market
 
Prestige Avon is located on Thanisandra Main Road, with connectivity to the Outer Ring Road and Kempegowda International Airport. The developer is positioning the project around the area's growing residential, commercial and social infrastructure.
 
Thanisandra has attracted residential development due to its proximity to employment hubs, including Manyata Tech Park, and its access to North Bengaluru's transport corridors. The location has also seen the launch of premium apartment projects catering to buyers seeking larger homes.
 
Prestige's recent launches in the city include Prestige Camden Gardens, Prestige Pine Forest and Prestige Somerville. Its Q4 FY24 investor presentation listed Somerville as a Bengaluru residential launch with 306 units. The company's Q4 FY25 investor presentation also listed Camden Gardens and Pine Forest among its Bengaluru residential launches. 
 
As of September 2026, Prestige Group said it had delivered 323 projects spanning 221 million sq ft and had a pipeline of 140 projects across 240 million sq ft. 
 
Key details of the project: 
  • Spread across approximately 3 acres, Prestige Avon comprises 260 apartments 
  • The project has an estimated gross development value (GDV) of approximately ₹5,500 million.
  • Offering a selection of 2 and 3 BHK residences, Prestige Avon also features home offices in select layouts
  • Apartment sizes range from approximately 1,306 sq. ft. to 2,160 sq. ft.
 
"Prestige Avon is designed for homebuyers looking for a well-connected address combined with thoughtfully planned homes and contemporary lifestyle amenities. Thanisandra has emerged as one of North Bengaluru’s key residential corridors, benefiting from strong connectivity and the continued development of the region. With its carefully planned residences, including select layouts with dedicated home-office spaces, Prestige Avon responds to the changing expectations of today’s urban homebuyer," said Irfan Razack, Chairman and Managing Director, Prestige Group.

data.title: Apple camera software chief Jon McCormack exits after eight years
data.description:
By Mark Gurman
 
Apple Inc.’s head of camera and photo software has left, marking a rare shake-up in the leadership behind one of the iPhone’s most important features. 
Jon McCormack retired at the end of October after more than eight years at the company, according to people with knowledge of the matter. He oversaw the Camera and Photos apps and the underlying technology that determines how users capture, view and edit their pictures and video.
 
Apple hasn’t named a new vice president to take over McCormack’s exact role. Instead, his former deputies are assuming his responsibilities under another executive, said the people, who asked not to be identified while discussing internal moves. An Apple spokesperson declined to comment. 
The departure represents a significant change for a critical selling point of Apple’s flagship product. The iPhone is widely considered the world’s most popular camera, with users taking trillions of photos and hundreds of billions of selfies each year. Improvements to photography and video are central to Apple’s marketing and help persuade consumers to upgrade.
 
 
McCormack played a key role in developing those features, overseeing work that requires close coordination between software engineers and Apple’s camera hardware and chip teams. Modern smartphone photography depends heavily on image processing and machine learning, making the software as integral to the experience as the lenses and sensors.
 
His work included the redesigned selfie camera introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup last year. This year, Apple added a variable-aperture camera to the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, giving users more control over lighting and depth of field. The company also introduced a customisable Camera app interface with professional controls.
 
His departure comes at a time when Apple is navigating a fundamental shift in photography. Competitors such as Alphabet Inc.’s Google and Samsung Electronics Co. have increasingly embraced generative AI features that allow users to make substantial changes to images. That has blurred the distinction between capturing a real moment and creating an artificial one. 
McCormack was a strong opponent of using generative AI to create or alter photographs, believing that images should represent moments that actually occurred, according to people inside the company who were familiar with his views. That philosophy has increasingly come into tension with Apple’s recent embrace of AI-powered tools. 
 
“A photograph is of something that actually happened,” McCormack told Wired earlier this year. “It’s really important to us that we create tools that keep the sanctity of that moment.” Still, the executive’s retirement wasn’t related to a disagreement or clash with Apple over its AI strategy, the people said.
 
Until early this year, McCormack reported to Craig Federighi, Apple’s senior vice president of software engineering, whose organisation is under pressure to accelerate AI development and deliver new capabilities more quickly. The retirement leaves Federighi overseeing a leadership transition in a highly specialised area.
 
The camera and photos software teams are now reporting to Sebastien Marineau-Mes, who oversaw the teams earlier in his career but is otherwise in charge of integrating AI features across the company’s operating systems. The camera team has key individual leaders, including Alok Deshpande. 
 
McCormack joins Jennifer Bailey, the longtime head of the Apple Pay and Wallet services, among the notable vice presidents to leave the company this fall. New Chief Executive Officer John Ternus also has undertaken management changes as part of a push to make the company faster and more efficient.

data.title: Asian stocks head for worst week since 2020 as AI rally loses steam
data.description:
Asian shares fell on Friday, heading for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in the AI sector, while the dollar extended a rally on safe-haven flows.

MSCI's broadest ​index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan lost 3.2 per cent, its biggest single-day drop in over a month. ​The gauge has now sunk 8.3 per cent this week, its worst performance since March 2020.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 4.1 per cent and was headed for a ‌6.8 per cent weekly drop, while South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.4 per cent and was set to end the week 7.1 per cent lower. Taiwan shares were down 5 per cent on Friday and 16 per cent for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1991.

 

The moves in Asia followed losses of more than 2 per cent for the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite after Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, saw its shares surge in a historic debut but the euphoria failed to lift other stocks.

"Risk aversion intensified as investors continued to unwind crowded positioning and reassess the broader macro backdrop following Anthropic's record-shattering IPO," said Preston Pagli, markets analyst at Citi.

He added that Nvidia's blowout earnings earlier in the week failed to become the reset markets had hoped for, while sentiment deteriorated further after Anthropic's IPO failed to spark a broader rally.

Further adding to the unease, a report on AMD from a media outlet associated with short-selling fund Hunterbrook Capital raised concerns that the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some ‌linked to blacklisted firms, could draw greater US regulatory scrutiny to the sector.

The AI trade has already been battered by Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, growing momentum for the anti-data-centre movement following Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections, and concerns over the sector's rising debt loads.

"No one headline drove the roll though some pointed to an AMD short report which tapered overall sentiment. Overall, it just felt like more questions than answers out there today with most wondering what gets this tape to feel better?" said Goldman Sachs analysts in a trading note.

They said asset managers and hedge funds net-sold macro products while they net-bought pockets of consumer and financials, with liquidity remaining poor, which is exacerbating price action.

US stock futures ​also pointed to further losses, with the S&P 500 futures down 0.2 per cent and Nasdaq futures down 0.6 per cent in Asia on Friday.

Dollar extends rally, Treasury yields ‌dip on risk aversion

As risk sentiment took a beating, the US dollar extended its rally on safe-haven bids, while also being supported by growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in, ​according to CME Group's ‌FedWatch tool.

The dollar index last traded steady at 103.86, after rising to its highest since April 2025 this week, and is now on track to post ‌its fourth week of gains.

In government debt, US Treasury yields eased as the sharp equity selloff pushed investors toward safe-haven bonds. The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes held steady at 5.02 per cent, near a one-week low. The 2-year yield touched 4.749 per cent, compared with a US ‌close of 4.779 per cent.

Oil ​prices were mostly ​steady after an earlier spike, as reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz offset pressure from rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus.

Brent crude futures rose 0.4 per cent to $92.37 a barrel but remained on track for a ‌third week of declines.

Non-interest-bearing gold ​slid 2.5 per cent to $3,533.40 an ounce and was headed for a 9 per cent weekly loss.

data.title: Visa, Mastercard, JPMorgan customer data exposed in ransomware attack
data.description:
Customer information linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase was exposed on Thursday after a ransomware group claimed to have stolen data, news agency Reuters reported. This adds to a series of technology disruptions that have raised consumer concerns over the past week.
 
The three companies said the breach did not affect their payment systems and that no customers' card payment details were compromised.
 
Several major organisations, including Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and the US National Security Agency (NSA), have reported problems with their computer systems and online services in recent days. Last month, cryptocurrency exchange Binance also suffered a major cyberattack
 
 

JPMorgan says third-party vendors targeted

 
JPMorgan Chase, the largest lender in the US, said on Thursday that cyber attackers had targeted third-party service providers working with the bank.
 
"Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names ‌and email addresses," a JPMorgan spokesperson told Reuters, adding that the company would contact the affected customers directly.
 
Earlier this week, JPMorgan faced problems processing transactions because of a software bug. The issue also affected other banks and led to disruptions in their services.
 

Ransomware group claims to have stolen customer records

 
The disclosure came after a cyber extortion group called "n0n" claimed on November 16 that it had accessed JPMorgan's cardmember engagement records. The information included "hundreds of thousands of campaign interactions for tens of thousands of distinct cardmember email addresses," according to a screenshot of the group's message captured by cybercrime research platform eCrime.ch.
 
A Reuters review of the leaked information found what appeared to be 124 email addresses belonging to bank employees and more than 16,000 customer email addresses. Some records also contained phone numbers and postal codes.
 
The same hacking group made similar claims involving Visa and Mastercard on November 16 and also published data that it said belonged to the two companies.
 

Visa, Mastercard say payment networks unaffected

 
Visa said it was aware of the claims and that the incident was linked to a third-party service provider in the Asia-Pacific region.
 
According to Reuters' review, the Visa data released by the hacking group mainly relates to customers in Asia-Pacific markets, including Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia, Australia and Macau. The information, spread across several spreadsheets, includes thousands of purported customer email addresses, phone numbers and details of Visa marketing campaigns.
 
The news report quoted a Mastercard spokesperson as saying that the company had recently been informed about an incident involving a third-party provider. The incident "resulted in the exposure of a limited amount of email addresses—non-payment information—from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit programme".
 
The spokesperson said there was no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards.
 
The Mastercard information shared by n0n includes marketing records linked to customers in North America, West Asia and Africa. It also contains email addresses belonging to a small number of Mastercard employees.

data.title: Rahul Gandhi says India has become a 'side player' in global affairs
data.description:
India always had a sophisticated understanding of geopolitics, but has become a side player in global affairs, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has said, citing the role Pakistan played in negotiating peace between the US and Iran.

"India, by its size, naturally has a global voice and India should be actively involved in global conversations. But frankly, India has become a side player," Gandhi said during an interaction with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday.

Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, said India has relationships with the US, Iran and Russia. "I'm pretty shocked that Pakistan is busy negotiating with the Iranians and the Americans, and India's just looking," he said.

 

He said that soon after Independence, India was the leader of the Non-Aligned Movement, which gave it a certain stature in the world, and he would love New Delhi to regain that voice on the global stage.

Gandhi also slammed the foreign policy pursued by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, which is based on personal relationships with global leaders such as US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Friendship is not the point. Who gives a damn about friendship? Do you really think that geopolitics is going to work because the guy is your friend? He's leading a structure. He's got a whole economic system under him. He's not going to make decisions based on whether he likes you or doesn't like you. So these are some of the things that disturb me," Gandhi said during the interaction moderated by Professor Robert Pape.

"I don't have a problem with being friends with Mr Modi or being friends with leaders. Friendship is not that important. What's important is that you understand what's going on, who you are, and where you fit," Gandhi said.

The Congress leader said the last security structure was built after World War II by one civilisation, the West, while the next one will be shaped by America, China, India, the Middle East and Russia.

"The next global architecture will not be built by one civilisation alone. It will be shaped by multiple civilisations, with America, China, India, the Middle East and Russia all having a role to play," he said.

Responding to a question from a Pakistani participant, Gandhi said peace talks with Islamabad can begin the moment it stops supporting and encouraging terrorism in India.

"Well, there is room, but there is a big problem, which is the support and encouragement of terrorism by Pakistan in our country," Gandhi said to a question on the possibility of the two neighbours moving beyond the blame game and working together.

"It is impossible for us to accept our innocent people being murdered and have a conversation with Pakistan. So, the moment that stops, a conversation can potentially begin," Gandhi said.

data.title: Trump admin cleared over 879k AI chip sales to Chinese firms: House panel
data.description:
The US Commerce Department authorised shipments of more than 879,000 advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May 2026, according to documents released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee on Thursday.
 
The approvals included 75,000 chips for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD. All four companies feature on the Pentagon's list of Chinese companies alleged to have links with the country's military, the committee said.
 
During the same period, companies sought permission to sell 3.4 million US-made AI chips to China, according to the documents, which cited applications from Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). The approved licences covered Nvidia's H200 chips and AMD's equivalent MI325X processors. However, it was not immediately clear how many of the approvals had resulted in actual shipments to China.
 
 
The disclosure of export licensing data comes as US President Donald Trump's administration faces heightened scrutiny over its approach to technology exports to China. The issue has also drawn attention following reports about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a Chinese spy, fuelling renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance on Beijing.
 
The Commerce Department said its approach to H200 licensing "is based on a rule published in the Federal Register in January 2026, which imposes significant additional national security-related requirements on license applicants in order to qualify for case-by-case consideration rather than a presumption of denial".
 

Committee invokes national interest to release chip export data

 
According to CNBC, a spokesperson for the Bureau of Industry and Security said the agency had shared details of both approved and rejected licence applications for Nvidia's H200 and comparable chips with Congress.
 
The House Foreign Affairs Committee invoked the Export Control Reform Act to justify releasing the data. The law allows the panel to declassify and disclose export information if it "determines that the withholding of the following information is contrary to the national interest".
 
The applications made public by the committee included requests involving major Chinese companies such as ByteDance and Baidu, as well as Tesla's Shanghai operations.
 

How have the companies reacted?

 
Nvidia said the approvals were subject to strict conditions and limited volumes. However, the company said it had since stopped shipping H200 chips to China despite receiving some licences. AMD, meanwhile, said it complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across its global operations, Reuters reported.
 

US tightens curbs on advanced chip exports

 
The latest disclosure comes amid broader efforts by the Trump administration to tighten controls on advanced chip exports and prevent Chinese companies from accessing computing capacity through overseas data centres.
 
On Monday, the administration announced fresh restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, tightening controls amid talks between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit, Reuters reported.
 
The new rule tightens restrictions on shipments of advanced chips to data centres in countries such as Thailand and Malaysia, which Chinese companies have used to access computing capacity for training AI models. It also introduces additional requirements for overseas data centres supplying "significant volumes of computing power" to companies headquartered in China.
 
During Trump's second term, the administration approved exports of Nvidia's H200 chips to China, reversing restrictions imposed under former President Joe Biden. However, questions remained over whether the approved chips were actually reaching Chinese buyers.
 
In May, Reuters reported that the US had cleared about 10 companies to purchase the H200 chips, but no deliveries had taken place at the time. In July, Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler told a congressional committee that shipments had since begun, although volumes remained very low. Several major Chinese internet companies had each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips.

data.title: Anthropic pares IPO gains as shares slide 5% in after-hours trading
data.description:
By Natasha Mascarenhas, Carmen Reinicke and Sangmi Cha
 
Anthropic PBC shares were down about 5 per cent in post-market trading as the artificial intelligence developer wrapped up its first day as a public company after a record-setting $107.3 billion offering. 
The late moves pared a debut pop of 17 per cent on Thursday, which provided a rare bright spot as the Nasdaq fell 2.2 per cent. The broader market continued on a downward trend into the Asian day, with global stocks poised for their longest losing streak in more than three years, as the AI trade cratered. 
 
While the bright open for the Claude chatbot maker reflected massive investor appetite after a heavily oversubscribed initial public offering, the steep valuation — combined with fresh competitive threats — weighed heavily in after-hours trading, highlighting jitters over how long that momentum can hold.
 
 
“With what appeared to be the final pillar supporting the AI rally now giving way, market sentiment is now very pessimistic,” said Gerald Gan, chief investment officer at Singapore-based Reed Capital. “While I am preparing to accumulate quality stocks at more attractive valuations, I am equally mindful of the risks of catching a falling knife.”
 
MSCI Inc.’s Asia Pacific equities index fell 3.4 per cent, extending its decline to a seventh session, and is poised for its lowest close since April. That pushed the MSCI All Country World Index — a key barometer of global stocks — on course for its longest losing streak since September 2023.
 
Against that backdrop, Anthropic’s IPO had attracted global demand for seven times the shares available for sale, with investors outside the US pouring in billions of dollars, including those in Japan securing $3 billion in stock after seeking $9.4 billion in shares and $1.1 billion of stock bought by mom-and-pop investors in the UK and continental Europe. 
The IPO vaulted Anthropic to the status of unrivaled AI industry leader — at least for the moment — and delivered billions of dollars in returns to its backers and pushed up the combined wealth of its seven founders to $166 billion. The record raise blasted by the $75 billion IPO record set in June by SpaceX, which ultimately totaled $86.25 billion with the so-called overallotment shares sold by the underwriters. Goldman Sachs Group Inc., Morgan Stanley and 20 other banks earned a record $550 million in fees for their work on Anthropic’s IPO.
 
Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut followed weeks of shaky trading in US stocks, which has left investors grappling with worries over Nvidia Corp.’s role as a major backstop of the AI ecosystem following its longtime chief’s ouster and a Democratic sweep in midterm elections that promises to change the industry’s regulatory landscape.
 
“You’ve seen sentiment sort of continue to worsen around AI and it has not let up today,” said Jordan Watson, managing director of investments at Tandem Investment Advisors. “What’s important for markets now is Anthropic is the most transparent real-time signal of the AI risk trade.”  
Anthropic closed at $97.17 Thursday in New York, paring an opening surge that took it as much as 39 per cent above the IPO price of $83. It ended the day as the world’s seventh-biggest public company with a fully diluted market value of about $1.8 trillion.
 
In a blow to sentiment, Apple Inc. said it is developing its own autonomous AI agent that can get things done on behalf of users, looking to enter a fast-growing market already being pursued by Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta Platforms Inc. and others.
 
Thursday’s broader market weakness was “just a continuation of what we’ve seen for the last several weeks, and that is a lot of nervousness around the semiconductor space,” said Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth. “The financing of the AI ecosystem is certainly a question that investors are asking and it’s weighing on the market at large.”
 
Some of the broader selloff may have also been fueled by investors selling positions in other companies to buy Anthropic shares, she added.  
The company won over investors with a focus on enterprise customers, propelling its run-rate revenue — a measure annualized from a shorter period — to $81 billion as of Oct. 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, its regulatory filings show.
 
Claude Code, the company’s coding agent for software developers, is widely adopted in the industry and has even been used by NASA engineers, the filing shows. Anthropic has more than 11,900 customers delivering $100,000 of revenue each on a trailing 12-month basis as of the end of September, up from about 1,500 in 2025.
 
The company aims to expand its footprint in more professions from law to healthcare. Anthropic counts Novartis AG CEO Vas Narasimhan as one of its board members.
 
A major challenge will be taming ballooning costs for AI infrastructure and reliably delivering operational profitability. Anthropic reported a $567 million operating loss in the third quarter, primarily driven by $5 billion of computing costs under short-term commitments and $2 billion of non-cash charges related to the company’s charitable donation-matching program.
 
“It popped like any other IPO on the first day but we will need to see solid results in the coming quarters, new use cases for AI, accelerating monetization etc to dispel the gloom in the AI trade,” said Vey-Sern Ling, managing director at Union Bancaire Privee. “Investors don’t have very many fundamental drivers to go on for Anthropic for now. A large part of the value is in the future, which is uncertain, so the share price movements will reflect that.”
 
Goldman Sachs Group Inc. research analysts expect the company to take until 2030 to generate positive free cash flow on an annual basis, Bloomberg News reported. That said, they are modeling Anthropic’s annual revenue to soar to roughly $685 billion by 2030, Bloomberg News has reported. To pull off that feat, it will need to fend off AI pricing pressures from cheaper open-weight models, including from Chinese developers.
 
Anthropic is expected to see a lift from index-tracking funds generating billions of dollars in demand. If it qualifies for early inclusion, it could join the Russell 1000 and the Nasdaq 100 as soon as December. FTSE Russell and Nasdaq changed their rules this year to speed the inclusion of large new listings.

data.title: Anthropic becomes world's 7th most valuable company with $1.8 trn valuation
data.description:
By David Morris

data.title: Gold ETFs down 5%; Silver ETFs plunge over 6%, trade at 52-week lows
data.description:
Gold, Silver ETFs crash on Friday as sell-off in precious metals deepens

Gold and Silver Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) cracked up to 6 per cent in Friday's intraday trade on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) as the sell-off in precious metals deepened. On the COMEX (United States), Gold futures traded up to 4 per cent lower around $3,530 levels, and Silver futures quoted around $41.60 levels - down nearly 6 per cent amid fears of a December Fed rate hike. Analysts reckon that a stronger US dollar, coupled with rising bond yields amid high inflation signals a likely rate hike in December. Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst-Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities believes that the overall sentiment remains weak, and volatility is expected to stay elevated in precious metals for  now. "Going ahead, the US Federal Reserve's December policy meeting will remain the key trigger, with dollar strength, inflation expectations and the Fed's policy guidance likely to determine the next directional move," says Trivedi. On the NSE, as of 9:30 AM on Friday, Nippon India Silver ETF (SILVERBEES) plunged 6.4 per cent to a 52-week low of ₹142.97 on trades of around 29 million shares. Meanwhile, Nippon India Gold ETF (GOLDBEES) shed 4.8 per cent at ₹101.21 with around 28 million shares changing hands at the counter on the NSE. GOLDBEES traded near its 52-week low of ₹100.61 touched on November 21, 2025. Among others, ICICI Prudential Gold ETF, 360 One Gold ETF and Axis Gold ETF were also down around 5 per each at ₹104.77, ₹120.25 and ₹102.05 levels, shows NSE data. ICICI Prudential Silver ETF, HDFC Silver ETF, SBI SILVER ETF and Zerodha Silver ETF also dipped over 6 per cent each to ₹149.15, ₹142.60, ₹146.75 and ₹15.08, respectively. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE 

Gold, Silver prices down up to 66% from all-time high

 Gold and Silver prices have cracked up to 25 per cent in the last two weeks on the COMEX. Gold prices plunged 25.3 per cent, and Silver dropped 20.4 per cent, shows data. Meanwhile, Silver prices have slumped up to 66 per cent from its all-time high of $121.785 registered in January 2026. Whereas, Gold is down 37.3 per cent from its summit. Back home, Gold ETFs have tumbled around 21 per cent in the last three straight months, and are down up to 33 per cent from their peaks. Whereas, Silver ETFs plunged around 35 per cent in the last three months, and are down up to 62 per cent from the record highs, shows data. On the technical charts, GOLDBEES is seen trading near its 100-week moving average, which stands at ₹102.25 for the first time since October 2022. On the other hand, SILVERBEES is quoting below its 100-WMA, which stands at ₹165.70, shows chart. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Titan, Muthoot Finance, Kalyan Jewellers fall up to 4% as Gold prices slide
data.description:
Gold-related stocks price performance

 
Gold related-listed companies including gold financiers and jewellery stocks were under pressure declining up to 4 per cent amid falling gold prices.
 
Titan Company, Kalyan Jewellers India, PC Jeweller, P N Gadgil Jewellers and Sky Gold and Diamonds from the jewellery stocks, and Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance from the gold financiers were down in the range of 3-4 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was down 0.33 per cent at 82,746.
 

Why are gold-related stocks under pressure?

 
Gold and silver prices remained under pressure amid continued strength in the US dollar and expectations of aggressive interest-rate increases by the Federal Reserve.
 
 
At 9.04 AM, the MCX December gold traded at ₹122,435 per 10 grams, down ₹5,017, or 3.94 per cent, from the previous close. 
 
Gold Prices have witnessed healthy softening from its peak levels in January 2026. In January 2026, the gold price/10gm stood at ₹1,81,000 which implies 32 per cent correction in prices for the period January-November 2026.
 
The domestic decline followed heavy international selling. Reuters’ November 20 morning report put December US gold futures at $3,551.90 an ounce, down 3.6 per cent.
 
ALSO READ | Gold ETFs down 5%; Silver ETFs plunge over 6%, trade at 52-week lows A dollar near a 19-month high and expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate increase are weighing on bullion. Analysts assess that forced liquidation was adding to the decline. The Indian sell-off is consistent with that international pressure, although the available figures cannot isolate the contribution of currency movements or domestic position closures, said Vikram Subburaj, CEO, Giottus.com.
 
Meanwhile, the recent correction in gold prices could result in inventory losses for jewellery companies, given the higher-cost inventory procured by jewellery companies prior to the customs duty changes, ICICI Securities said in a note.
 
However, lower gold prices are likely to improve consumer sentiment and affordability, supporting buyer growth and driving a gradual recovery in gold jewellery demand. The growth momentum in the studded segment is expected to sustain. 
 
Overall, this along with better product mix will help earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) margin Titan’s Jewellery business adjusted EBIT margins to remain in the 11–12 per cent range, driven by favourable mix and better operating leverage. Further, the revenue growth of most jewellery players is likely to moderate in H2FY27 due to a high base in H2FY26. Any further correction in gold prices could provide an incremental boost to buyer growth and would help large jewellery players to gain share in key markets, the brokerage firm said.
 
Jewellery companies stock prices have witnessed correction in past few days and any further correction will provide a buying opportunity in quality jewellery stocks (including Titan and BlueStone Jewellery & Lifestyles), ICICI Securities said.
 
Further, a sharp fall in gold prices is negative for gold finance companies like Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance because their loans are backed by gold collateral. A fall in gold prices erodes the loan-to-value (LTV) cushion on the secured book.
 
Analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services in its Q2 result update said, it believes near-term asset-quality trends of Muthoot Finance remain uncertain as customers adapt to the revised repayment structure, necessitating higher collection efforts.
